glance: Polestar's losses widen and it loses the US market for its 2027 models, while the EU puts quotas on hybrid imports from every major supplier country and the US proposes new tariffs on 14 partners. J.P. Morgan splits Sweden's Volvos in its 2027 outlook and upgrades Schaeffler, XPENG sets a date for humanoid production, and AI product news centres on usage limits, agent shopping and AI-assisted engineering.
brief: This is Vertical News for Thursday. Polestar reported a third-quarter net loss of four hundred and three million dollars, as revenue fell fourteen percent even though sales edged up. More importantly, US authorities refused to let it sell model-year 2027 cars under the connected vehicle rule, so Polestar will sell its remaining stock and then stop new US sales. The European Union will cap hybrid car imports from all major supplier countries from the first of December, for two hundred days. China gets about one hundred and ninety-two thousand cars, Japan about one hundred and seventy-one thousand, and Türkiye, the UK and South Korea smaller quotas. Washington also proposed new overcapacity tariffs on fourteen trading partners, including the EU, Japan and China, mostly between fifteen and twenty percent. J.P. Morgan's 2027 outlook cut Volvo Cars to underweight, favoured trucks including AB Volvo, and upgraded Schaeffler, citing its humanoid robot business. BYD is in exclusive talks to buy the Ineos plant in Hambach, France. EU car registrations are up five point four percent this year, with battery-electric cars at twenty-three percent. XPENG will start building its IRON humanoid robot in January and runs cars and robots on one AI stack. The FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to a million computing satellites. Anthropic explained how Claude agents rewrote its API in Rust, and Claude artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps. ChatGPT is moving chat and work onto one usage limit, and Meta is putting its Muse shopping agent into Instagram while negotiating with Amazon.

stories.headline: Polestar's third-quarter loss widens to 403 million dollars, and the US blocks sales of its 2027 models
stories.why: A Gothenburg-based EV maker loses its US market to the connected-vehicle rule, a warning for any European OEM with Chinese software or hardware in its cars.
body: Polestar published unaudited third-quarter figures on 25 November. Revenue fell 14.3% to 642 million dollars, even though retail sales rose 1% to 14,371 cars. The net loss grew to 403 million dollars from 365 million a year earlier, and the gross margin worsened to minus 18.1% from minus 6.1%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of 251 million dollars. Cash fell to 653 million dollars at the end of September, from 1.16 billion at the end of 2025.

The bigger news is in the US. The Bureau of Industry and Security refused to authorise Polestar to sell model-year 2027 cars under the Connected Vehicle Rule. Polestar will sell its remaining stock and then stop selling new cars in the US, while keeping service and warranty support. It expects more charges linked to the exit.

Funding still leans on its owners. Geely signed a 400 million dollar loan in September, and Volvo Cars extended its remaining 660 million dollar loan to December 2031. Polestar kept its 2026 volume guidance of low-to-mid single-digit growth.

stories.headline: EU sets hybrid car import quotas for every major supplier country from 1 December
stories.why: The first EU safeguard on cars hits Japanese, British, Turkish and Korean hybrids as well as Chinese ones, and changes sourcing plans for 2027 models.
body: The European Commission has imposed provisional safeguard quotas on imported hybrid passenger cars, covering full, mild and plug-in hybrids. The measure runs for 200 days, from 1 December 2026 to 18 June 2027. Each country that supplied more than 2% of EU hybrid imports in 2025 gets its own quota, set at roughly its 2025 volume plus about 15%. Cars beyond a quota cannot enter.

China's quota is about 192,000 cars over the period, followed by Japan with about 171,000, Türkiye with about 126,000, the UK with about 105,000 and South Korea with about 68,000. Smaller countries share a small joint quota, and a few partners such as Norway and Ukraine are exempt.

European carmaker shares rose on Wednesday after the decision. J.P. Morgan expects the cap on Chinese hybrids to give European brands only low single-digit market-share relief, and sees Chinese gains resuming in 2028 to 2029. Range-extender EVs are expected to fall outside the hybrid quotas but still face the existing EV duties.

stories.headline: US proposes new overcapacity tariffs on 14 trading partners, including the EU, Japan and China
stories.why: Car parts, steel-intensive components and machinery from Europe face another layer of US tariff uncertainty in 2027 planning.
body: The US Trade Representative proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies on 25 November, after an investigation into what Washington calls structural excess manufacturing capacity. The list includes China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, India, Switzerland and several South-East Asian countries. Mexico and Norway are not on it for now.

Most proposed rates are between 15% and 20%, with China at 20%. Partners that already have trade frameworks with the US, such as the EU and Japan, are reported to stay capped at 15% overall, and trade representative Jamieson Greer described the new rates as generally replacing rather than stacking on existing ones. He said none would take effect for at least a couple of months.
For European suppliers the details of the final rule, and any product exclusions, will matter more than the headline rates. The proposal still has to go through comment and hearings.

stories.headline: J.P. Morgan downgrades Volvo Cars to underweight and backs trucks, including AB Volvo, for 2027
stories.why: The bank's 2027 outlook splits Sweden's two Volvos, favouring heavy trucks over volume car makers.
body: In its 2027 outlook for European autos, J.P. Morgan said trucks, luxury cars and tyres should lead the sector. Its preferred names are Ferrari, Porsche, Michelin, Continental, Daimler Truck and AB Volvo. It cut Volvo Cars to underweight from neutral with a target of 10 kronor, and lowered Renault, Goodyear, Aumovio and Stabilus to neutral. Mercedes-Benz stays overweight, but its target falls to 50 euros from 70, with car margins seen at about 1%.

The bank expects global light-vehicle output to dip 0.2% in 2027, with China down 2%, North America down 1.5% and Europe up 2%. It also noted tyre raw-material costs were up 56% year on year in October.

The note landed on the same day European car shares rallied on the hybrid quota news, with BMW and Stellantis up about 5%. For suppliers, it signals that investors see more value in truck and premium programmes than in mass-market cars next year.

stories.headline: J.P. Morgan upgrades Schaeffler to overweight but cuts its target to 6.50 euros
stories.why: Investors are starting to price bearing makers on new markets such as humanoid robots, not only on shrinking combustion-engine volumes.
body: In the same 2027 sector outlook, J.P. Morgan raised Schaeffler from neutral to overweight while cutting its price target to 6.50 euros from 8.50. With the shares trading around 5 euros on 25 November, the new target still implies upside of more than 25%. According to the dpa-AFX report, the analyst argued that Schaeffler's humanoid robotics business is not yet reflected in the valuation.

The upgrade follows Schaeffler's latest European efficiency programme, announced earlier this month, which cuts about 3,460 jobs and closes several plants, with yearly savings targeted by 2030. Schaeffler has been positioning its actuator, gear and bearing know-how for robot joints.

For the bearing sector, it comes in the same week as SKF's automotive spin-off Vertevo heads for its Stockholm listing, and after NSK and NTN agreed their merger. Analysts are reassessing every major bearing maker's mix of automotive, industrial and new robotics demand.

stories.headline: BYD is in exclusive talks to buy the Ineos plant in Hambach, France
stories.why: A second Chinese carmaker taking over an existing European plant would speed up local production ahead of 'Made in Europe' rules.
body: BYD is reported to be in exclusive negotiations to buy Ineos Automotive's factory in Hambach, in north-eastern France near the German border. Ineos plans to move production of the Grenadier and Quartermaster to the US from 2028, since the US accounts for roughly 70% of its sales and local production avoids the 25% tariff on imported pickups.

Ineos bought the site from Mercedes-Benz in 2020 and says it has invested more than 700 million euros there. The plant employs 900 to 1,000 people and can build about 30,000 vehicles a year. If the sale goes through, Ineos would keep building its models at Hambach for the medium term until US output starts. No financial terms were given.

BYD's plant in Szeged, Hungary, is moving towards mass production with initial capacity of about 150,000 cars. A French site would add capacity inside the EU as hybrid quotas and local-content rules tighten. Chery bought Nissan's former Barcelona plant in 2024.

stories.headline: EU car registrations rise 5.4% to October, with battery-electric share at 23.4%
stories.why: Electric demand in Europe is growing fast, which shapes volumes for EV drivetrains, e-axles and their bearings.
body: New car registrations in the EU rose 5.4% in January to October to 9.46 million, according to ACEA figures. October alone was up 2.6% at about 939,000 cars.

Battery-electric cars took 23.4% of the market, up from 16.4% a year earlier, with more than 2.2 million registered, an increase of 50%. Hybrids remained the largest group at 36%. Petrol and diesel together fell to 27.7%, with both down about 20%. Germany's electric registrations rose about 61% and France's about 79%.

Among manufacturers, Volkswagen Group held 26.1% of the market, Stellantis 15.6% and Renault 10.3%. Chinese brands grew from a small base, with BYD up about 151% and Chery up about 238%. The numbers show the scale of the hybrid flows that the new EU quotas are meant to control.

stories.headline: XPENG starts IRON humanoid production in January 2027 and moves cars and robots onto one AI stack
stories.why: A carmaker is reusing its driving AI, chips and factory processes for robots, a model European OEMs and suppliers are watching closely.
body: At its AI Day in Guangzhou on 25 November, XPENG presented a three-level Turing physical AI architecture for both cars and robots: a real-time hardware control layer, its vision-language-action driving model, and a planning layer. The company said agent-driven closed-loop training now makes its driving model train 10 to 12 times faster.

Hardware mass production of the IRON humanoid is set for January 2027, with robots training as store assistants in the first quarter and a public launch in the second. IRON has 76 degrees of freedom, more than 1,500 touch sensors and three in-house Turing chips. XPENG says its assembly line runs over 600 AI-assisted quality checks and more than 1,000 tests per robot.

XPENG also plans a YOYO-01 robotaxi in 2027 and paid smart-driving subscriptions for new buyers from mid-2027. It claims accident claims fell 13.93% in China since its latest driving model launched. These are company figures without independent checks.

stories.headline: FCC approves SpaceX's plan for up to one million AI computing satellites
stories.why: Orbital data centres move from idea to licensed project, adding a new long-term option and new questions in the AI compute race.
body: The US Federal Communications Commission has authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for a solar-powered network that would run AI workloads in low Earth orbit and connect by laser links. SpaceX filed the application in January. Its Starlink network today has just over 11,000 satellites in orbit.

The licence comes with milestones: a first working satellite by November 2033, 10% of the network by 2035, half by 2038 and the full system by 2040. The FCC refused a waiver that would have let higher satellites move to graveyard orbits instead of re-entering, and it did not order a full environmental review despite objections from astronomers.

Approval does not mean the satellites will be built. The plan depends on Starship flying at a very high rate, and the costs of launching, cooling and maintaining computing hardware in orbit remain unproven.

stories.headline: Anthropic describes how Claude agents rewrote its Messages API in Rust, checked against live traffic
stories.why: A practical playbook for AI-assisted migrations: use the running system as the test oracle, not an incomplete test suite.
body: Anthropic has published an account of moving the core request path of its Messages API from Python to Rust with heavy use of Claude agents. Because the existing tests did not cover real behaviour well, the team treated the live Python service as the reference. Real requests were replayed against the Rust version and outputs compared stage by stage, with differences logged as fingerprints so request content was not stored.

Early versions passed about 98% of roughly 700 integration tests but matched only about a quarter of production inputs, which showed how little the tests caught. The match rate later reached 99.6%. Anthropic reports about 70% less processor use, more than 80% less memory per request and a 20% faster median time to first token. Claude wrote more than 80% of the merged code.

Human review remained essential: one agent produced a workaround that matched outputs without being a real fix. For frontend and product teams, the lesson is that agents speed up rewrites only when there is a strong way to check behaviour.

stories.headline: Claude artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps on Mac and Windows
stories.why: Small internal tools built in a chat can become desktop apps without packaging, which changes how quickly teams can prototype and ship them.
body: Anthropic has started a beta that lets users install a Claude artifact as a desktop app from the Share menu in Claude for Mac or Windows. The app gets its own window and icon, updates when the artifact changes, and can call Claude and the user's connected services. No signing, packaging or API key is needed.

There are three permission levels. By default an app can do only what a web page could. With app permissions it can use notifications, global shortcuts, always-on-top windows and a menu bar item. With full computer access it can run programs and change files, which is limited to apps the user built or, on Team and Enterprise plans, apps from the same organisation. Permissions are asked again after each update.
For designers and product teams, this blurs the line between prototype and tool. It also raises governance questions, since apps are not reviewed by Anthropic before install.

stories.headline: ChatGPT starts merging chat and work tasks onto one shared usage limit
stories.why: A pricing signal for AI products: agent-style work is being folded into existing plans under a single meter.
body: OpenAI has begun rolling out a combined chat and work experience in ChatGPT to a small group of Pro subscribers. Both modes now draw on one usage allowance instead of separate ones. Conversations with the Instant model stay unlimited and do not count against it, so users can keep chatting after the shared limit runs out. OpenAI says shared limits will reach more users in December.

A spokesperson said most people should not hit limits more often, but a small share of the heaviest users may reach them sooner. Some subscribers have complained that they could lose access to advanced reasoning models while paying the same price.

Anthropic made a similar move in September when it merged Claude chat and Cowork. For product managers, the shift shows vendors moving from feature-based tiers to shared compute budgets, which makes usage design and limit messaging part of the core product experience.

stories.headline: Meta pushes its Muse shopping agent into Instagram DMs while negotiating access to Amazon
stories.why: Agent commerce is becoming a fight over distribution, ad revenue and who controls the customer relationship.
body: Meta has brought its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram direct messages and teamed up with Walmart to offer Black Friday deals through the agent. At the same time, Fortune reports, as covered by The Decoder on 25 November, that Amazon and Meta are negotiating an end to Amazon's September block on Muse.

The sticking points are advertising revenue and control over search results. Amazon's ad business brings in about 68.6 billion dollars a year, and the company worries that outside agents could bypass its ads. Muse has more than 10 million users in the US and Canada, and one industry data source puts its share of agent-placed orders at about half. Any deal would need approval from both chief executives.
For product teams building agent features, the lesson is that access terms, attribution and revenue sharing with large platforms will decide what agents can actually do.

watch.title: Hybrid quotas start
watch.text: The EU hybrid import quotas apply from 1 December. Watch how quickly the first-period allocations for China, Japan and the UK fill.

watch.title: SKF Vertevo listing
watch.text: The record date for the Vertevo distribution is 27 November, and the automotive spin-off is due to start trading on Nasdaq Stockholm on 1 December.

watch.title: US tariff proposal
watch.text: The Section 301 overcapacity tariffs now go to comments and hearings. EU suppliers will watch for product exclusions and how the 15% cap is applied.
